title: URDF-Anything+: End-to-End Generation for Simulation-Ready Articulated Assets
claim: Prior methods chain multiple segmentation, retrieval and parameter-prediction stages; ours generates the complete output end-to-end in one autoregressive process.
layout: 3 panels: prior (left), ours (middle), advantages column (right); checkmarks
description: A wide figure with three regions. The left rounded panel, titled 'Previous Methods', shows a tangled multi-stage workflow. A text prompt and an image feed an image-to-3D model that produces a point cloud. VLM and 3D segmentation models then produce bounding boxes, part text, mesh retrieval, point-cloud segments and token segments. These feed a VLM or decoder that outputs part parameters and a URDF file. The middle panel, 'URDF-Anything+ (Ours)', is a cleaner flow. An image goes to a mesh model, which conditions a DiT that autoregressively emits parts at timesteps t=0 to 3, from SOT to EOT. The output is a URDF file that goes to a simulator and a robot policy. The right green column lists four advantages with green checkmarks: end-to-end, simpler structure, lower inference cost, and better simulation-ready URDF. Pastel blue, yellow and pink boxes carry the color coding.
caption: Comparison between previous methods and our method. In (a), we summarize previous generation paradigms for articulated objects, including different segmentation approaches and joint parameter generation methods. In (b), we briefly illustrate our method and its advantages.
abstract: Articulated objects are fundamental for robotics, simulation of physics, and interactive virtual environments. However, recovering them from visual observations is inherently challenging, as images provide only partial and ambiguous cues about both part geometry and their underlying kinematic structure. Existing approaches typically rely on multi-stage pipelines, retrieval from asset libraries, or explicit part segmentation. We present URDF-Anything+, an end-to-end autoregressive diffusion framework that generates simulation-ready URDF models directly from a single RGB image. Conditioned on visual observations and object geometry, URDF-Anything+ operates in a structured latent space and jointly models part geometry and articulation in a unified generation process. Specifically, the model sequentially predicts each articulated part together with its associated joint parameters, while a termination token dynamically determines the number of parts. This design enables direct generation of fully executable URDFs without external retrieval or post-processing stages. Experiments on large-scale articulated object benchmarks demonstrate that URDF-Anything+ outperforms prior methods in geometric reconstruction quality, joint parameter estimation, and physical executability, while being substantially more efficient than existing multi-stage approaches. Furthermore, the generated URDFs serve as faithful digital twins, enabling the zero-shot transfer of manipulation policies trained purely in simulation.
